title: Espaces stratifiés et voisinages côniques (ou : déploiement des espaces stratifiés) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Section 17 opens a recapitulation of the neighbourhood and tube objects attached to a stratified space with index poset I. These are V_i (the tube around stratum X_i), V_{i0…in} (indexed by flags), V_Σ, V_J^L and V_{J,L} (indexed by complementary pairs J, L = I∖J). The section announces a generalisation V_{J0,J1,…,Jn} indexed by chains of subsets. This page lays the order-theoretic groundwork.

For a poset I, a subset J is 'fermé' if it is downward closed (j∈J, i≤j ⇒ i∈J). Down-sets are stable under arbitrary intersections and arbitrary unions; Grothendieck corrects 'finies' to 'quelconques'. They are therefore the closed sets of a topology on I, the 'lower topology'. This is the Alexandrov topology in the convention where the closure of {i} is the down-set ↓i.

This is exactly the convention that makes the stratification map X→I continuous when \bar X_i = ∪_{j≤i} X_j (frontier condition).
- (82): the closure of A is its down-closure, \bar A = {i | ∃ j∈A, i≤j}.
- J is closed iff L = I∖J is open iff L is an up-set, i.e. closed for the topology attached to the opposite order (the 'upper topology').
- (83): closure in the upper topology is the up-closure \tilde B = {i | ∃ j∈B, i≥j}. This is also the smallest open set of the lower topology containing B, an Alexandrov-specific feature: every point has a minimal open neighbourhood ↑i.
- J is locally closed (closed ∩ open) iff J = \bar J ∩ \tilde J.

The next page names such J 'bandes' (order-convex subsets). It defines a domination preorder on subsets, J ≺ K iff J ⊂ \bar K and K ⊂ \tilde J, whose quotient is the set of convex subsets. It characterises J ≺ K for bands by the existence of a band I' = \tilde J ∩ \bar K in which J is closed and codense and K is open and dense.

The purpose is to replace flags i0<…<in of strata by chains J0 ≺ J1 ≺ … ≺ Jn of convex pieces of the stratification. This allows multi-tubes V_{J0,…,Jn} around unions of strata, generalising the V_{J,L} attached to an open/closed decomposition I = J ⊔ L.
errors: No mathematical errors. Grothendieck's own correction of 'réunions finies' to 'réunions quelconques' is right: down-sets are closed under arbitrary unions, which is the Alexandrov property.

The equivalence 'locally closed ⇔ J = \bar J ∩ \tilde J' relies on \tilde J being the smallest open set containing J. This holds in the Alexandrov topology, and the page states it, so the argument is complete.

ideas.what: Topology on the index poset whose closed sets are the down-sets (and dual upper topology); closure = down-closure, smallest open neighbourhood = up-closure
ideas.modern_name: Alexandrov topology on a poset; stratification as a continuous map X → P to a poset with its Alexandrov topology
ideas.usually_credited_to: P. Alexandroff (1937) for the topology; its use to define stratified spaces is usually credited to Lurie (Higher Algebra, App. A.5, ~2009–2017)
ideas.where_published: Not in EGA/SGA as such. Esquisse d'un programme discusses tame stratified spaces but not, to my knowledge, this formalism.

ideas.what: Locally closed subsets of a poset in the Alexandrov topology = order-convex subsets ('bandes'), J = \bar J ∩ \tilde J
ideas.modern_name: order-convex subsets / intervals; locally closed unions of strata
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore in order theory and stratified topology

ideas.what: Planned indexing of tubular/conic neighbourhood data by chains J0 ≺ … ≺ Jn of convex subsets under a domination preorder, generalising flags of strata
ideas.modern_name: closest: coarsenings of stratifications / décollages and homotopy links indexed by chains of strata (Barwick–Glasman–Haine; Haine; Nand-Lal; Ayala–Francis–Tanaka)

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets up stratifications indexed by a poset carrying its Alexandrov topology ('top. inférieure'), with closed = down-sets. This matches the convention now standard after Lurie, where a P-stratified space is a continuous map X → P. The page shows Grothendieck using this framework around 1981–82 for his theory of tame stratified spaces.
missed.quote: ce sont donc aussi les fermés d'une top. sur I, appelée sa top. inférieure
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is an earlier, unpublished instance of the modern foundational convention for stratified spaces and exit paths. It is of historical rather than mathematical interest.

missed.claim: Announced construction of neighbourhood objects V_{J0,J1,…,Jn} indexed by chains of convex subsets under domination J ≺ K. This would amount to functoriality of the 'déploiement' with respect to coarsening of the stratification and to multi-stratum links.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Compatibility of homotopy links with coarsenings (merging strata into convex blocks) is studied in modern exodromy and stratified homotopy theory. Grothendieck's domination preorder on convex subsets is a concrete combinatorial device that could be compared with these treatments.

deep.surprise_reason: The page itself is elementary order topology (Alexandrov topology, convex = locally closed). Its interest is only as evidence that Grothendieck used the poset-with-Alexandrov-topology framework for stratifications and planned chain-indexed neighbourhood objects, which are developed on later pages.
transcription_corrections: 'fermé pour la top. associée : l'ordre opposé : I admi[?] de I' should read approximately 'fermé pour la top. associée à l'ordre opposé à celui de I'.
'ce sont donc {+aussi+} [-les-] fermés' should read 'ce sont donc aussi les fermés'. The crossed-out word appears to be 'ces', not 'les'.
In the line on L, the struck-through fragment before 'i≥l' looks like an aborted quantifier; the intended text is 'i.e. l∈L, i≥l ⇒ i∈L'.
'stable par [-intersecti-], quelconques' should most likely read 'stable par intersections quelconques' (possibly rewritten), since the sentence requires intersections.
